name: Singapore
summary: Rules depend on the origin's AVS schedule. Schedule I (AU, NZ, IE, UK): no quarantine. Schedule II (e.g. USA, Canada, Japan, Hong Kong, most of Western Europe, New Caledonia): no quarantine if the pet arrives within 5 days of the owner and has lived with them for 6+ months, otherwise at least 10 days of quarantine. Schedule III (everywhere else): at least 30 days at the Animal Quarantine Centre (AQC). Every pet needs a dog/cat licence and an AVS import licence.
microchip: ISO 11784 or ISO 11785 Annex A. The chip number must appear on all vaccination and treatment records.
vaccinations: Rabies (Schedule II and III only): valid inactivated or recombinant vaccine, with no lapse in cover. Schedule I pets need no rabies vaccine or serology.
Dogs: canine distemper, adenovirus type 1, parvovirus type 2.
Cats: feline calicivirus, herpesvirus-1, panleukopaenia.
Schedule III pets are vaccinated against rabies again on arrival at AQC.
rabies_titer: Schedule II and III: rabies serology of at least 0.5 IU/ml. The blood sample must be taken at least 28 days after a valid vaccination, and between 90 days and 12 months before export. The lab must be a WOAH reference lab or one approved by the competent authority of a Schedule I or II country.
parasite_treatment: Parasite treatments and the veterinary health certificate must both be done 2 to 7 days before export, as set out in the schedule-specific veterinary conditions.
documents: Dog licence or cat licence (PALS), obtained before the import licence
AVS import licence via GoBusiness (valid 90 days, cannot be extended)
Veterinary health certificate in the schedule-specific format: Sections I-III by the treating vet, Section IV endorsed by an official government vet, issued 2-7 days before export
Vaccination records and rabies serology report
Signed captain's declaration endorsed by the airline (Schedule I/II)
Customs GST In-Payment permit where applicable
Inspection appointment booked at least 5 days before arrival via AVS e-services
import_permit: Yes: an AVS import licence (personal: S$50 normal, 2 working days; S$100 express, 1 working day), valid 90 days. The dog or cat licence must be obtained first. The USDA summary says to apply 30 days before arrival.
quarantine: Schedule I: none. Schedule II: none if the pet arrives less than 5 days after the owner's entry and has lived at the owner's address for 6+ months; otherwise at least 10 days of home quarantine (smart collar, S$29/animal/day, apply via FormSG first) for personal imports, or 10 days at AQC for commercial imports. Schedule III: at least 30 days at AQC (Sembawang), booked through the Quarantine Management System once the serology result is ready.
timeline: Plan at least 4-7 months for Schedule II/III (serology must be at least 90 days before export), and about 1 month for Schedule I. Steps: microchip, rabies vaccine, serology (28+ days after vaccine), book AQC if Schedule III, dog/cat licence, import licence, book inspection 5+ days before arrival, vet certificate and treatments 2-7 days before export.
restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs: Pit Bull types (American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier, American Bulldog), Akita, Boerboel, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Neapolitan Mastiff, Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, and crosses of any of these. Cats: F1-F4 Bengal or Savannah crosses are prohibited. Housing limits apply (e.g. HDB flats). Minimum age 12 weeks at export.
private_aviation: AVS describes air clearance only at the Changi Animal & Plant Quarantine Station (Changi Airfreight Centre). In-cabin or excess-baggage pets must be in a rigid IATA crate (no soft bags). AVS does not mention Seletar or private aircraft. One FBO arrival guide (Universal Aviation, not official) says pets are accepted at Seletar under the same AVS licence and inspection rules. Confirm with AVS and the FBO where the inspection will happen before routing to Seletar.
export: AVS publishes separate 'Exporting dogs and cats' procedures (avs.nparks.gov.sg). Not reviewed in detail here.
authority: Animal & Veterinary Service (AVS), National Parks Board (NParks)

name: Malaysia
summary: A MAQIS import permit is needed. Pets from 'scheduled' countries (list updated by DVS on 11 Dec 2025) can enter without quarantine. Pets from all other countries need a rabies vaccination before export and at least 7 days of quarantine on arrival, which DVS can extend up to 6 months. Sabah and Sarawak have their own state veterinary authorities and rules.
microchip: ISO 11784/11785-compliant microchip required under the DVS regulations for non-scheduled countries.
vaccinations: Rabies (non-scheduled countries): approved vaccine before export. The DVS pet portal says at least 30 days before entry.
Other core vaccines given within 12 months before export, as recommended by a licensed vet.
rabies_titer: Not required in the DVS regulations for Peninsular Malaysia (antibody levels may be tested at random during quarantine). Sabah and Sarawak may differ; not verified.
documents: MAQIS import permit (ePermit)
Pet passport or certificate with full description and identification

Veterinary health certificate from the exporting country's government veterinary authority: examination within 7 days before export, no rabies in the country for the previous 6 months, not imported into the country within the previous 6 months
Rabies vaccination certificate
Scheduled countries: Malaysian veterinary certificate and airline captain's affidavit (per DVS portal)
import_permit: Yes: MAQIS import permit. Restricted dog breeds also need prior written approval from the MAQIS Director General.
quarantine: Non-scheduled countries: at least 7 days in quarantine, which can be extended up to 6 months case by case. Scheduled countries: no quarantine per the DVS pet portal. Scheduled list (DVS notice of 11 Dec 2025): United Kingdom, Eire, Northern Ireland, New Zealand, Japan, Sweden, Brunei, Singapore, Greece, Luxembourg, Czech Republic, Malta, Slovenia, Estonia, Bahrain, Austria, Belgium, Germany, Portugal, Montenegro, Bulgaria, Lithuania. Australia appeared in the older list but is not in the Dec 2025 list; confirm with DVS.
timeline: Plan at least 6-8 weeks before travel: microchip, rabies vaccine (30+ days before entry), MAQIS permit, government-endorsed health certificate within 7 days of export, then quarantine on arrival unless from a scheduled country.
restricted_breeds: Banned dogs: Akita, American Bulldog, Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Neapolitan Mastiff, Pit Bull types (American Pit Bull Terrier, American Staffordshire Terrier, Staffordshire Bull Terrier). Restricted dogs (need MAQIS approval, pedigree, premises inspection, personal pet or security use only): Bull Mastiff, Bull Terrier, Doberman, German/Belgian/East European Shepherd, Perro de Presa Canario, Rottweiler. Minimum age 3 months.
private_aviation: The DVS regulation says pets must be carried by aircraft or other transport directly to the prescribed landing place or any other airport in Malaysia. No rule specific to private aircraft was found. Confirm the arrival airport and the quarantine officer's attendance with MAQIS/DVS.
authority: Department of Veterinary Services (DVS) and Malaysian Quarantine and Inspection Services (MAQIS). Sabah and Sarawak: state veterinary departments (Sarawak: dvs@sarawak.gov.my)

name: Thailand
summary: Apply to the Animal Quarantine Station (AQS) at the arrival airport for a DLD import permit, at least 7 and no more than 60 days before departure (30 days recommended). The pet needs a government-endorsed health certificate and is inspected at the AQS on arrival. There is no titre test and normally no quarantine when documents are complete.
microchip: Microchip number required on the application and records. The DLD advises implanting it before or on the same day as the rabies vaccination.
vaccinations: Rabies: at least 21 days before departure for a primary vaccine, given at 12 weeks of age or older. Boosters need no wait. Pets from rabies-free countries may be exempt.

Dogs: distemper, hepatitis, parvovirus, leptospirosis. If the leptospirosis vaccine is not valid or not 21+ days old, a negative leptospirosis test within 30 days before departure is accepted instead.
Cats: feline panleukopenia.
documents: Application Form R.1/1 with pet details and microchip implantation certificate
Copy of owner's passport and flight itinerary
Colour photo of the pet
English vaccination certificates
Official health certificate endorsed by the exporting country's veterinary authority (US: valid 10 days from USDA endorsement; originals only)
Printed import permit; Form R-6 and Import License R-7 issued at the AQS on arrival (500 THB per animal)
import_permit: Yes: DLD import permit, emailed by the AQS at the port of entry. Processing takes 5-7 Thai business days and the permit is valid 60 days. Owners travelling with their pet may apply on arrival if all originals are ready, but airlines may refuse boarding without a permit.
quarantine: No fixed quarantine when documents are complete. The pet is inspected at the AQS on arrival. If documents are incomplete, the pet may be held at the quarantine station.
timeline: Plan at least 5-6 weeks: microchip, vaccines (21+ days before applying), permit request 30 days before departure, health certificate and endorsement within 10 days of arrival.
restricted_breeds: The Thai Embassy (Washington) says no dog breeds are banned, but airlines may restrict some. Minimum age 4 months (USDA summary).
private_aviation: AQS offices are at Suvarnabhumi, Don Mueang, Chiang Mai, Phuket, Samui and Krabi (all 24 hours for hand-carried pets; the Suvarnabhumi cargo AQS is open 08:30-16:30 Mon-Fri). The permit names the port of entry. No rule specific to private jets was found. Coordinate the arrival airport's AQS inspection and the FBO in advance.
export: DLD: the microchip must be implanted before or on the same day as the rabies vaccine. Present the pet and documents at the departure port's quarantine station, ideally 2-3 days before departure, to get the export certificate.
authority: Department of Livestock Development (DLD), Animal Quarantine Stations

name: Philippines
summary: Every dog and cat needs an SPSIC import clearance from the Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), applied for online through the DA Trade System (11 working days), and current rabies vaccination. Personal imports are limited to 3 animals per importer per year. From 1 January 2027 a rabies antibody titre test becomes mandatory for all applications.
microchip: Microchip required (number recorded on the SPSIC and used to track repeat imports). Pets arriving without the required identification are refused entry and returned (consular sources).
vaccinations: Rabies: given by a licensed vet in the source country at 12 weeks of age or older. After a first-ever vaccination, wait 14 days before applying. Annual boosters: can ship at once if given within the vaccine's validity, otherwise wait 14 days. 3-year vaccines are accepted.
Rabies may be waived for pets from WOAH self-declared rabies-free countries.
BAI says only rabies vaccination is required.
rabies_titer: Not currently required. Mandatory for all SPSIC applications from 1 January 2027 (BAI). Test details (lab, timing, wait) were not yet published on the pages reviewed.
parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatment records are uploaded with the application. They need not be renewed before applying, but must remain valid until arrival.
documents: SPSIC (BAI import clearance)
Vaccination and antiparasitic records
Microchip number and an actual photo of the pet
Pet passport if any
Veterinary health certificate from the origin country matching the SPSIC (animal count must match)
One-time importers: notarised Affidavit of Undertaking (BAI MC 43, 2020)
import_permit: Yes: SPSIC from BAI via the DA Trade System. Processing takes 11 working days and the permit is valid 60 days (BAI FAQ). A permit issued after the pet's departure date is invalid. A new permit is needed if the airline changes in transit.
quarantine: BAI's pet import page sets no quarantine. The pet is inspected at the port of entry.
timeline: Plan at least 6-8 weeks (more for 2027 arrivals because of the titre test): microchip, rabies vaccine (14-day wait if first dose), SPSIC application (11 working days), health certificate, travel within SPSIC validity.
restricted_breeds: Minimum age 4 months. No pregnant animals. Animals that have given birth must have done so at least 12 weeks before travel. No breed bans found on BAI pages.
authority: Bureau of Animal Industry (BAI), National Veterinary Quarantine Services Division

name: Indonesia
summary: The USDA certificate for Indonesia requires a rabies vaccination, a rabies antibody (FAVN) result of 0.5 IU/ml or more, 6 months' residence in the exporting country, and a vet exam within 5 days of departure. Barantin's import procedure, quarantine length and authorised entry airports could not be confirmed officially. Bali is reported to bar dog and cat imports, but this is unverified.
microchip: Microchip number is recorded on the USDA certificate.
vaccinations: Rabies: killed vaccine, pet at least 3 months old (USDA certificate for Indonesia).
rabies_titer: FAVN result of 0.5 IU/ml or more (USDA certificate). The official sources reviewed give no wait period or sample timing.
documents: Government-endorsed veterinary health certificate: exam within 5 days of departure; no rabies reported in the area where the pet lived for the last 6 months; 6 months' residence in the exporting country
Rabies vaccination and FAVN results
Barantin import/quarantine documents (not verified)
import_permit: Barantin (Indonesian Quarantine Agency) handles pet entry through its PTK Online system. Permit details were not confirmed from official sources.
quarantine: Not confirmed officially. Secondary sources cite 7-14 days at a Barantin facility.
timeline: Plan at least 3-4 months (vaccine, FAVN, permit), and confirm with Barantin first.
private_aviation: Unverified secondary sources say pets must enter through designated airports such as Jakarta (CGK), not Denpasar (DPS). Bali (rabies-affected) is reported to prohibit dog and cat imports under a provincial regulation. Do not route pets to Bali without written Barantin and Bali provincial confirmation.
authority: Indonesian Quarantine Agency (Badan Karantina Indonesia, Barantin)

name: Australia
summary: Group 1 (New Zealand, Norfolk Island, Cocos (Keeling) Islands): no quarantine. Group 2 (rabies-free) and Group 3 (approved, rabies absent or well controlled) countries need a DAFF import permit (BICON) and Post Entry Quarantine at Mickleham, arriving into Melbourne. Pets from non-approved countries must first live in an approved country.
microchip: Microchip required; identity is tied to the RNAT. For Group 3, a competent-authority (official government vet) identity check before the RNAT blood draw cuts quarantine from 30 to 10 days.
vaccinations: Rabies (Group 3): vaccination valid from the RNAT blood draw through export.
Other vaccines and tests per the import permit.
rabies_titer: Group 3: RNAT by FAVN or RFFIT, at least 0.5 IU/ml. Export only 180 days or more after the lab receives the sample. The RNAT is valid 12 months from sampling; a retest plus a permit variation avoids restarting the 180 days.
parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatments per the permit and step-by-step guide (timings not verified here).
documents: DAFF import permit (BICON)
RNAT declaration and lab report (Group 3)
Competent-authority identity check (optional, enables 10-day quarantine)
Government-endorsed veterinary health certificate
Dogs (per USDA summary for US origin): tests for Leishmania infantum, Brucella canis (unless desexed), Leptospira Canicola (unless vaccinated)
PEQ booking confirmation
import_permit: Yes for Group 2 and 3, via BICON. Secondary sources say permits typically take 20-40 business days (sometimes much longer).
quarantine: Group 2: at least 10 days. Group 3: at least 10 days only if the competent-authority identity check was done before the RNAT blood draw and at least 180 days before export; otherwise at least 30 days. All quarantine is at the Mickleham PEQ facility (Melbourne). Book only after the permit is issued, via the Post Entry Biosecurity System or by phone (1800 900 090). The facility accepts arrivals 05:00-14:30 Mon, Tue, Sat, Sun and 05:00-21:00 Wed-Fri.
timeline: Plan at least 7-8 months for Group 3: identity check, RNAT blood draw, wait 180 days (meanwhile the permit takes 20-40+ business days), book Mickleham after the permit, pre-export tests, treatments and certificate, then fly into Melbourne. Group 2 is shorter (weeks to a few months).
restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terrier/American Pit Bull Terrier, Perro de Presa Canario. Some cat hybrids (e.g. Savannah) are prohibited. Verify on DAFF.
private_aviation: Allowed with conditions. Pets normally arrive as manifested cargo directly into Melbourne (no domestic transfers). For a private or chartered flight, DAFF must be told before departure: the permit must be varied (fees apply), and DAFF gives written approval after a document check before the flight leaves. Group 2/3 flights must land at a first point of entry airport in Victoria. The pet must be crated before the aircraft enters Australian territory and stay crated until it reaches PEQ. On mixed flights, Group 2 pets stay sealed the whole flight; Group 3 pets may be uncrated until Australian territory.
export: Export certification is through DAFF (MICoR lists destination requirements; export health certificates are government-endorsed). Group 3 pets returning to Australia can use the identity check on their Australian export certification.
authority: Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry (DAFF)

name: New Zealand
summary: Pets from Australia (Category 1) need no quarantine. Pets from Category 2 (rabies-free) and Category 3 (rabies absent or well controlled) countries need an MPI import permit, a pre-booked quarantine place, and at least 10 days of quarantine. They must arrive by air as manifested cargo at Auckland or Christchurch only. Non-categorised countries are not eligible directly. A new Import Health Standard (2026) applies alongside the 2021 one until 31 March 2027 and is mandatory from 1 April 2027.
microchip: Microchip required. 2026 IHS official identity check: Category 2, microchip scanned by an official vet at least 6 months before shipment. Category 3, official scan before the RNATT sample (twice, the first at least 6 months before shipment, if the RNATT is taken 3-6 months before shipment). Mandatory for all arrivals from 1 April 2027; the ID check process started on 1 October 2026.
vaccinations: Rabies (Category 3): at 12 weeks of age or older, continuously valid; a primary vaccination must be at least 6 months before shipment (2026 IHS).
Category 2: no rabies vaccination required.
rabies_titer: Category 3 (2026 IHS): RNATT of at least 0.5 IU/mL on a sample taken 3-12 months before shipment.
parasite_treatment: 2026 IHS: internal parasites treated twice (first within 30 days of shipment and at least 14 days before the second; second within 5 days of shipment). Ticks and fleas: last treatment within 16 days of shipment with continuous protection. Dogs also need heartworm prevention and tests for Babesia gibsoni, Brucella canis (entire dogs), Leishmania, leptospirosis and others, per the IHS.
documents: MPI import permit
Signed quarantine booking form
Category 3: rabies vaccination records, RNATT result, Category 3 Rabies Certification Form
Pre-export ID check notified by the exporting competent authority directly to MPI
Government-endorsed veterinary certificate; vet exam within 2 days of shipment
import_permit: Required for Category 2 and 3 (including assistance dogs). Book quarantine first and attach the booking form. Allow 30 working days after all documents are received (USDA says at least 20 business days).
quarantine: At least 10 days at an MPI-approved transitional facility for Category 2/3, longer if extra tests or treatments are needed or the period ends outside business hours. Book before the permit application. Australia and assistance dogs are exempt.
timeline: Plan at least 7-8 months for Category 3 (6-month ID check, RNATT 3+ months before shipment, quarantine booking, then permit 30 working days) and 6-7 months for Category 2 (6-month ID check). Australia: weeks.
restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Brazilian Fila, Dogo Argentino, Japanese Tosa, Perro de Presa Canario, American Pit Bull Terrier type. Hybrid dogs and cats (other than Bengal) need EPA approval. Approximate minimum ages: 8 weeks (Category 1), 12 weeks (Category 2), 9 months (Category 3). Not more than 42 days pregnant.
private_aviation: The 2026 IHS says a cat or dog arriving by air must travel as manifested cargo (only assistance dogs excepted) and may arrive only at Auckland or Christchurch. Category 2 crates must carry a government seal. MPI has no specific private-aircraft guidance. A pet in the cabin of a private jet does not meet the IHS, so arrange manifested-cargo status with MPI before booking.
export: NZ-origin pets need the MPI veterinary (export) certificate or Animal Welfare Export Certificate (AWEC), which is also required to re-enter as an 'NZ-origin' pet. Short trips of 30 days or less use a simplified short-stay certificate.
authority: Ministry for Primary Industries (MPI), Biosecurity New Zealand

name: Fiji
summary: A Biosecurity Authority of Fiji (BAF) import permit is required; the conditions in it depend on the origin country. Pets must go straight from arrival into mandatory Post Entry Quarantine (PEQ) at Koronivia, which must be booked at least 1 month ahead.
microchip: Required: readable by AVID, TROVAN, DESTRON or an ISO-compatible reader.
vaccinations: As specified in the permit, by origin country.
rabies_titer: Set by the permit according to origin; not stated on the BAF page.
parasite_treatment: Treatments and their intervals are specified in the permit.
documents: Original BAF import permit (valid 6 months)
Home-country health certificate
Veterinary certificates with all lab results
Vaccination records
Microchip proof
import_permit: Yes. Apply to BAF (animalimports@baf.com.fj) and pay the fee on lodgement. Processing takes about 5 working days and the permit is valid 6 months.
quarantine: Mandatory PEQ at Koronivia, Nausori. The minimum period is set by BAF/permit (not stated on the page). Book at least 1 month before arrival. Guide and service dogs may be exempt case by case.
timeline: Plan at least 2-3 months (longer if origin requires rabies serology): apply for the permit, book PEQ 1+ month ahead, complete tests and treatments per the permit, notify BAF Nadi and the Chief Veterinary Officer before arrival.
restricted_breeds: Prohibited: Dogo Argentino, Fila Brasileiro, Japanese Tosa, Pit Bull Terriers (including American Pit Bull Terrier and crosses); serval cats and serval hybrids within 5 generations. Pets under 4 months and females more than 21 days pregnant are not allowed.
private_aviation: BAF requires the most direct route, intact crate seals, and confirmation that the aircraft carries no animals from other countries. Notify BAF Nadi Airport (+679 6720053) and the CVO (+679 3312512) in advance. No explicit private-jet rule was found; confirm with BAF.
authority: Biosecurity Authority of Fiji (BAF)

name: New Caledonia
summary: Direct import is allowed only from France, Germany, Sweden, Switzerland, Belgium, French Polynesia, Wallis and Futuna, Fiji, Vanuatu, Australia and New Zealand, with an import permit and a country-specific health certificate. Arrivals then spend 10 days in public quarantine at Païta. Pets from any other country must first spend 6 months in France, or go through quarantine in Australia or New Zealand.
vaccinations: Per the country-specific health certificate.
rabies_titer: Required per the certificate where applicable, and only at a DAVAR-listed approved laboratory (results from other labs are refused). Timing not stated on the page.
documents: Import permit (form I.DPA.NC.15/12)
Country-specific dog or cat health certificate
Rabies antibody result from an approved lab where required
Brachycephalic breeds: vet fitness-to-fly certificate and larger crate
import_permit: Yes, for every dog or cat import (SIVAP/DAVAR).
quarantine: 10 days in public quarantine (CPZP, Païta) on arrival for domestic carnivores from France or Pacific countries. For other origins the length is set by species and origin; confirm with SIVAP (+687 41 25 36, davar.sivap-qsa@gouv.nc).
timeline: Plan at least several months (6+ months for non-listed countries routed via France): permit, certificate, approved-lab titre where required, book quarantine.
restricted_breeds: No breed ban was listed on the DAVAR page. A brachycephalic breed list carries flight-welfare conditions.
authority: DAVAR – Service d'inspection vétérinaire, alimentaire et phytosanitaire (SIVAP)

name: French Polynesia
summary: An import permit from the Direction de la Biosécurité (online, about 7 months before departure) is required. Pets from non-rabies-free countries also need a rabies titre with a 3-month wait, dogs need a leishmaniasis test, and pets get two parasite treatments. Dogs and cats must travel as manifested cargo, with inspection at Tahiti only. Category 1 dogs are banned.
microchip: Identification certificate showing the implantation date is required.
vaccinations: Rabies: a primary vaccination is valid from 21 days after injection. Boosters must be given before the previous one expires, with the same vaccine.
rabies_titer: For non-rabies-free origins: blood taken at least 1 month after vaccination, at an accredited lab. The result is valid from 3 months after sampling, for 1 year. Pets vaccinated at 3 months cannot enter before 9 months and 21 days of age.
parasite_treatment: Internal and external parasite treatments by a vet: first within 30 days of departure (no later than 16-19 days before), second at least 14 days later and within 4 days of departure.
documents: Import permit (mes-demarches.gov.pf; 5,500 XPF per animal)
Identification certificate
Rabies vaccination certificates
Rabies titre result
Dogs: negative leishmaniasis ELISA/IF within 30 days of departure, sent directly to DBS (the permit is issued only after this)
Females: non-pregnancy ultrasound within 30 days of departure, or a sterilisation certificate
Official export health certificate signed within 4 days of departure
import_permit: Yes, online at mes-demarches.gov.pf (separate procedures for air and sea arrivals). Apply about 7 months before departure. Without a direct flight, each leg needs its own application.
quarantine: No quarantine period is stated. The pet gets an inspection and laissez-passer by the DBS official vet at Tahiti (fees about 6,000-12,500 XPF depending on arrival time).
timeline: Plan at least 7 months: microchip, rabies vaccine, titre (1+ month after the vaccine, then a 3-month wait), permit application, leishmaniasis test and parasite treatments in the last 30 days, health certificate within 4 days of departure.
restricted_breeds: Category 1 dogs (attack dogs under French classification) are prohibited. Pets under 3 months are not admitted unless with their mother. Snub-nosed breeds may be refused by airlines.
private_aviation: DBS states that dogs and cats must travel to French Polynesia as manifested cargo in sealed IATA crates; only certified assistance dogs may travel in the cabin. Inspection is done only at Tahiti. Private aircraft are not specifically addressed; a pet in the cabin of a private jet does not meet the stated rule. Confirm with DBS (zoo.aeroport.dbs@administration.gov.pf).
export: DBS publishes a separate page for exporting a pet from French Polynesia (not reviewed in detail).
authority: Direction de la Biosécurité (DBS), Cellule zoosanitaire

name: Cook Islands
summary: The Ministry of Agriculture publishes dog and cat import conditions only for New Zealand and Australia. Pets need a Biosecurity permit, an official government vet certificate, and must arrive by air as manifested cargo. Dogs also need a Police permit and must be desexed. No route was found for pets from other countries.
vaccinations: Dogs from NZ: distemper, hepatitis and parvovirus 1-3 months before export (parvovirus at 17+ weeks of age).
parasite_treatment: Dogs from NZ: praziquantel (5 mg/kg) and a roundworm/whipworm anthelmintic within 3 days of departure; two insecticidal washes 7 days apart, the last within 3 days of departure; free of ectoparasites (especially ticks) at the exam within 3 days of departure.
documents: Biosecurity import permit (Application Form for Live Animal)
Exporter's statutory declaration: 6 months' residence (or since birth), at least 4 months old, disease-free for 30 days
International animal health certificate signed by a full-time government vet of the exporting country
Dogs: Police import permit
import_permit: Yes: from the Director of Biosecurity, Ministry of Agriculture (biosecurity@cookislands.gov.ck, +682 28710). Dogs also need a Police permit.
quarantine: The pet is inspected and treated on arrival and held in the biosecurity area until a Permit to Land is issued. No fixed quarantine period is stated.
timeline: Plan at least 3 months: permits (Biosecurity and Police), vaccines 1-3 months before export, treatments and government vet exam within 3 days of departure, and flight details to Biosecurity at least 1 working day before shipping.
restricted_breeds: Prohibited dogs (Police, Dogs Registration Amendment Act 1991): Doberman, Pit Bull Terrier, Bull Dogs, Rottweiler, plus any breed the Police specify. All imported dogs must be neutered or spayed and registered with the Police.
private_aviation: The conditions require import only by air as manifested cargo. No private-aircraft provision was found; confirm with Biosecurity.
authority: Ministry of Agriculture – Biosecurity Service, Cook Islands
